title: Ideal powers times a coherent module give finite type Rees graded sheaf data
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], $J=I\mathcal O_X$ the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $F$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $G_m=J^mF$ be the image module with its inclusion $j_m:G_m\to F$, including the zeroth power [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Write $B=\mathcal R_A(I)$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra], $B_k=I^kt^k$ [def-nagata-rees-piece]. There exist maps $\mu_{m,k}:B_k\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(G_m,G_{m+k})$ such that on every open $U$, $j_{m+k}(\mu_{m,k}(b)(s))=f^\sharp(\operatorname{coeff}_k b)|_U\,j_m(s)$. Every $G_m$ is quasi-coherent, $\mu_{m,k}$ is additive, $\mu_{m+l,k}(b)\circ\mu_{m,l}(b')=\mu_{m,k+l}(bb')$ after the canonical degree identification, and $\mu_{m,0}(a)$ is multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$. For each $x\in X$ there are an open $U\ni x$, finitely many degrees $d_i$ and sections $s_i\in G_{d_i}(U)$ such that for every $V\subseteq U$, $t\in G_m(V)$ and $y\in V$, some open $y\in W\subseteq V$ has $t|_W$ in the $\mathcal O_X(W)$-span of the sections $\mu_{d_i,m-d_i}(b)(s_i|_W)$ for $d_i\le m$ and $b\in B_{m-d_i}$.

proof.text: Properness gives locally finite type; Mathlib supplies local Noetherianity of X. Apply the coherent/quasi-coherent finite-type equivalence to F. Prove quasi-coherence of J^m by two-step induction, starting with O_X and J, and prove quasi-coherence of G_m using the tensor multiplication image. The image is isomorphic to the kernel of its cokernel.
Obtain the multiplication maps and their section formula from the strictly smaller multiplication theorem, which requires only quasi-coherence, not finite type, properness or Noetherianity.

Each ideal-product inclusion is a categorical image inclusion, hence monic and sectionwise injective. For additivity, apply the inclusion and use the coefficient formula, polynomial coefficient additivity, and add_smul. For composition, compare both morphisms after their inclusions into F; rewrite the three coefficient formulas, write both homogeneous polynomials as monomials, and apply monomial multiplication, coefficient evaluation, map_mul and mul_smul. A private cancellation helper eliminates the equal target degrees before cancelling the mono, giving HEq. For degree zero, evaluate the formula on the image of a∈A, use its constant polynomial coefficient, and move the scalar through the linear inclusion. The base-map restriction identity is definitional.
Apply the degree-zero local generation theorem to F and the coefficient formula. Choose the original theorem’s degree function constantly zero and retain its generating sections and span witnesses.
